title: Interactive pin conflict resolver and inline performance annotations for version selection
creator: Priya Nair
description: Summary: Add an interactive conflict resolution UI and inline performance annotations to the Console version selection flow so teams can safely pin model versions during onboarding and publishing of performance profiles. Problem: when multiple users or automated rollouts attempt to pin different model versions simultaneously the Console currently shows a generic error and users must manually reconcile which version to keep. Separately, performance profiles (latency, cost-per-token, 95th latency, and quality eval snapshots) are published to the model catalog but are hard to compare at the moment of pin selection. Goals: 1) Surface recommended pins during model onboarding using the latest published performance profile and a simple delta UI. 2) If a concurrent pin conflict occurs, show an interactive resolver: side-by-side candidate comparison, a short timeline of recent pins, and a one-click resolution (choose candidate, merge metadata, or open a staged rollout). 3) Record audit log entries and link the selected performance profile to the pin. 4) Teach users during onboarding by surfacing a short explainer on how performance profiles influence runtime choice and cost. Scope: Console UI changes (version selection modal, timeline scrubber, inline annotations), API additions for conflict metadata (atomic pin attempt id, conflicting attempt payload), small backend contract to support merge/rollback decisions, and design assets for the resolver flows. Out of scope: implementing autoscale behavior or runtime kernel changes. Expected owner groups: PM (Priya), Design (Diego), Eng runtime & console (Samir Patel, Lin Zhao).
acceptance_criteria: When two pin attempts conflict, the Console displays a resolver modal with: (a) side-by-side summary of candidate versions, (b) published performance profiles for each, (c) a timeline of last 5 pins with timestamps and authors.

The resolver UI allows 3 actions: Accept candidate A, Accept candidate B, or Start a staged rollout (percentage-based). Each action triggers a documented API call and produces an audit log entry visible in the model activity feed.
Performance annotations (latency median, p95, cost-per-token, eval-quality delta) are shown inline in the version picker and are sourced from the latest published profile for each version.

Onboarding flow: new model onboarding checklist surfaces a recommended pin with rationale computed from performance profile and traffic characteristics; user can accept or open resolver if another active pin exists.
Design sign-off: Figma prototype linked in 'links' is reviewed and approved by Design and PM (comment thread below).
Backend contract: ENG-5201 implements atomic pin API with conflict payload; Console consumes it and handles status codes per documented spec.
End-to-end QA: simulated concurrent pin attempts during staging reproduce resolver flow; regression tests added to console e2e suite.
Telemetry: events emitted for resolver open, action selected, and final pin result. Metric goal: reduce manual pin reconciliation tickets by 60% in quarter after launch.
notes_and_decisions: 2026-02-14: Decided to prefer a lightweight in-Console resolver rather than a full chat-based arbitration flow to minimize scope and supportability.
2026-02-18: Trade-off: show only top-level performance metrics (median, p95, cost-per-token, eval delta) instead of full time-series in resolver to keep cognitive load low.
2026-02-25: Security note: pin actions require existing RBAC 'pin:modify' permission; attempt metadata will be recorded in audit logs for compliance.
2026-02-28: Engineering constraint: backend must return stable conflict id to allow re-fetching conflict state; ENG agreed to add endpoint in ENG-5201.
comments: 2026-02-12 - Samir Patel: Flagging ENG-5201 and ENG-5342 as critical. We need atomicity and an endpoint to fetch current pin state plus last-applied profile snapshot. Backend estimate: 3 sprint points.

2026-02-15 - Diego Alvarez: Uploaded initial Figma frames for resolver modal. Link in 'links'. Requesting feedback on the side-by-side card layout; also proposing a compact 'quick-accept' action for experienced users.
2026-02-20 - Priya Nair: PM feedback: add an onboarding microcopy explaining why a recommended pin was chosen (cost vs latency trade-off). Also include a CTA to view the full profile history.

2026-02-24 - Lin Zhao: Eng review: prefer optimistic UI for quick accept, but ensure server-side validation prevents race conditions. We will show a transient 'optimistic accepted' state and then confirm after API returns.
2026-02-27 - Security (Avery Chen): Confirmed no extra encryption needed; audit logs already capture pin user and timestamp but we'll add conflict metadata per compliance request.
